geneset_master_table_msigdb.geneset_id: MSigDB gene-set identifier — primary key and join key to gene_geneset_association_msigdb.geneset_id and geneset_metadata_msigdb.geneset_id. Internal opaque string; not user-queryable directly.
geneset_master_table_msigdb.geneset_name: MSigDB gene-set / signature name. The SOURCE database / ontology is encoded as the NAME PREFIX before the first underscore: HALLMARK_ (Hallmark), GOBP_ / GOMF_ / GOCC_ (Gene Ontology biological-process / molecular-function / cellular-component), REACTOME_, KEGG_ (KEGG_MEDICUS_*), BIOCARTA_, WP_ (WikiPathways), PID_, HP_ (Human Phenotype Ontology), MIR_ (microRNA targets). Real examples on disk: 'HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS', 'GOBP_RESPONSE_TO_X_RAY', 'REACTOME_ACTIVATION_OF_NMDA_RECEPTORS_AND_POSTSYNAPTIC_EVENTS', 'KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_TRANSCRIPTIONAL_ACTIVATION_BY_ACETYLATION_OF_H3K27', 'WP_GLYCOLYSIS_IN_SENESCENCE'. To find ALL gene sets from a given source DB / ontology (e.g. 'KEGG pathways', 'all GO biological-process terms', 'REACTOME gene sets', 'WikiPathways'), MATCH THIS COLUMN BY PREFIX (geneset_name LIKE 'KEGG_%', 'GOBP_%', 'REACTOME_%', …) — the source DB is NOT a `collection` value. Users may ask for 'gene set', 'signature', 'geneset name', or 'pathway name'. Note: geneset_id is the true unique key; the same geneset_name may appear multiple times within an organism (876 cases: 869 Mus musculus M-prefix vs MM-prefix pairs, 5 Homo sapiens anomalous MM-prefix IDs (MM17, MM1334-MM1337), 2 Rattus norvegicus pairs). Filter by geneset_id for unambiguous joins.
geneset_master_table_msigdb.collection: MSigDB collection in friendly-name form. The 10 observed values on disk are: Hallmark, Positional, Curated, Regulatory, Computational, Ontology, Oncogenic, Immunologic, CellType, CellLineage. Both human and mouse gene sets use these SAME friendly names (mouse sets cover Hallmark, CellType, Curated, Immunologic, Ontology, Positional, Regulatory; rat sets are Curated only). Users may ask for 'collection', 'MSigDB category', 'Hallmark', 'Curated', 'Ontology', etc. IMPORTANT: source databases / ontologies (KEGG, REACTOME, GO / GOBP / GOMF / GOCC, BIOCARTA, WikiPathways / WP, PID, Human Phenotype / HP, microRNA / MIR) are NOT `collection` values — they live in the geneset_name prefix and in sub_collection (e.g. 'CP:KEGG_MEDICUS', 'CP:REACTOME', 'GO:BP'). Route 'KEGG / REACTOME / GO / BIOCARTA / WikiPathways …' queries to geneset_name (prefix LIKE) or sub_collection, NEVER to collection. Note: legacy category CODES (H, C1–C9, MH, M1…) do NOT appear in any served table — the preprocess translates every code to its friendly name. collection is stored only on this master table (normalized out of geneset_metadata_msigdb).
geneset_master_table_msigdb.url: MSigDB URL for the gene set. Null for ~21.4% of sets (11,237); filter with col.is_not_null() before using as a link.
geneset_master_table_msigdb.gene_count: Number of unique genes in the set, stored as a String (e.g. '131'; observed numeric range 5–1998). Users may ask for 'gene count', 'set size', or 'number of genes'. Exactly 6 gene sets have a NULL gene_count (M40000, M41754, M41755, M41756, M45033, M45034) — these are zero-member sets (no rows in gene_geneset_association_msigdb) from upstream mapping failures; exclude them when listing member genes.
geneset_master_table_msigdb.geneset_organism: Organism the gene set was defined for. Observed values: 'Homo sapiens' (~34k sets), 'Mus musculus' (~18k sets), 'Rattus norvegicus' (~31 sets). Users may ask for 'organism', 'species', 'human', or 'mouse'.

gene_geneset_association_msigdb.geneset_id: MSigDB gene-set identifier — FK to geneset_master_table_msigdb.geneset_id. Join key only; not user-queryable directly. Join to geneset_master_table_msigdb for geneset_name / collection / organism / gene_count / url.
gene_geneset_association_msigdb.gene_id: Member gene of the set — FK to gene_master_table_msigdb.gene_id, the composite '<gene_symbol>|<organism>' key (e.g. 'MYC|Homo sapiens'). Join key only; filter/display the symbol via gene_master_table_msigdb.gene_symbol. This table is the normalized membership edge (one row per gene×geneset); it carries ONLY the two FK ids — gene_symbol, collection and organism are NOT stored here, they join from their master tables.

gene_master_table_msigdb.gene_id: Composite primary key '<gene_symbol>|<organism>' (e.g. 'MYC|Homo sapiens') — unique join key and FK target for gene_geneset_association.gene_id. The bare gene_symbol is NOT unique (17,458 symbols occur under more than one organism), so the composite is required to keep the membership join 1:1. Join key only — filter/display via gene_symbol / organism.
gene_master_table_msigdb.gene_symbol: HGNC (human) or MGI (mouse) gene symbol of a gene that appears in at least one MSigDB gene set (e.g. MYC, EGFR, TP53, KRAS, BRCA1). Users may ask for 'gene', 'gene symbol', or 'HGNC symbol'. Master catalog of all gene symbols indexed in MSigDB.
gene_master_table_msigdb.gene_organism: Organism for this gene symbol entry. Observed values: 'Homo sapiens', 'Mus musculus', 'Rattus norvegicus'.

geneset_metadata_msigdb.geneset_id: MSigDB gene-set identifier — FK / join key to geneset_master_table_msigdb.geneset_id. This is the per-geneset detail table (publication, source, descriptions); join to geneset_master_table_msigdb on geneset_id for geneset_name / collection / organism (NOT stored here — normalized to the master).
geneset_metadata_msigdb.historical_name: Historical or legacy name for the gene set. Effectively unused in the 2026.1 snapshot (100% null/empty); retained for schema completeness.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.pmid: PubMed ID of the source publication. Users may ask for 'PubMed ID' or 'PMID'. NULL (35,042 of 52,429 sets) when no publication is associated; filter with col.is_not_null() before use.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.authors: Authors of the source publication. NULL (35,034 of 52,429 sets) when unavailable; filter with col.is_not_null() before use.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.geo_id: GEO dataset identifier the set was derived from (e.g. 'GSE12345'). Users may ask for 'GEO ID' or 'GEO accession'. NULL (44
geneset_metadata_msigdb.exact_source: Exact upstream source or dataset (e.g. Ensembl genome annotation for Positional sets, KEGG pathway ID for Curated:KEGG_MEDICUS, figure/table citation strings like 'Table 2' or 'Fig. 6A' for Curated:CGP). Vocabulary varies by collection. NULL for 6,324 of 52,429 sets (12.1%); filter with col.is_not_null() before use.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.external_url: External URL for additional information about the gene set. NULL (11,237 of 52,429 sets) when unavailable; filter with col.is_not_null() before use.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.chip: Annotation platform or identifier used to define gene-set membership (e.g. 'Human_NCBI_Gene_ID', 'Mouse_NCBI_Gene_ID', 'HUMAN_GENE_SYMBOL'). Useful for interpreting how genes were mapped.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.sub_collection: Sub-collection — the PRECISE source DB / category within the parent collection (lives only in geneset_metadata_msigdb). Observed values on disk: CGP (chemical & genetic perturbations), CGN, CM (cancer modules), CP (canonical pathways, unsourced), CP:BIOCARTA, CP:KEGG_LEGACY, CP:KEGG_MEDICUS, CP:PID, CP:REACTOME, CP:WIKIPATHWAYS, GO:BP, GO:CC, GO:MF, HPO, IMMUNESIGDB, MIR:MIRDB, MIR:MIR_LEGACY, MIRDB, TFT:GTRD, TFT:TFT_LEGACY, GTRD, 3CA, MPT, VAX. This is the exact discriminator for source-DB queries: 'KEGG canonical pathways' → sub_collection LIKE 'CP:KEGG%'; 'GO biological process' → sub_collection='GO:BP'; 'Reactome pathways' → 'CP:REACTOME'; 'BioCarta' → 'CP:BIOCARTA'. (For a simple list/count of a source DB's sets, filtering geneset_name by prefix on geneset_master_table avoids the metadata join.) Users may ask for 'sub-collection', 'KEGG', 'Reactome', 'GO BP', etc.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.contributor: Person who contributed the gene set.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.brief_description: Short description of the gene set. Users may ask for 'description' or 'brief description'.
geneset_metadata_msigdb.full_description: Full free-text description of the gene set. Users may ask for 'full description'. Null for ~34.3k of 52
geneset_metadata_msigdb.tags: Tags for the gene set. Effectively unused in the 2026.1 snapshot (100% null/empty); retained for schema completeness.
